page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dadsv7 family. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is dedicated, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3780 GB of local disk space, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ads_v7 demonstrates strong computational capabilities. Single-core performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance under stress-ng and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the top 25% tier. Memory performance is also notable, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier, and uncached read and write memory bandwidth tests placing in the top 25% tier.

Database and inference benchmarks highlight specific workload alignments. PassMark database operations rank in the top 10% tier, and Redis SET operations achieve top 25% tier performance, supported by the large local storage capacity. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds for small and medium models rank in the top 10% and top 25% tiers respectively. However, a performance tradeoff is observed with larger models, where LLM inference speed for a 70B model drops to the middle 50% average tier, indicating limitations for heavy model execution without dedicated GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring high local storage density and balanced compute-to-memory resources.
